title: fix(console): paint a boot indicator during the pre-React white frame
body:
Fixes #2628

Tier 1 only, exactly as triage scoped it: give the white-frame window a visible
indication. Tier 2 (parallelising init / cache-skipping the init screen) and
tier 3 (whether init must block first paint) are untouched; two things I
measured on the way out are filed as separate cards at the bottom.

## 1. The premise, re-measured first — it holds

The card's numbers are from **2026-07-17**, ~40 days stale, and the dispatch
ordered a re-measurement before any code. Done, on this repository's own
production build. **The white frame is still there and still material**, so
this is a fix rather than a close.

### Method

`apps/console` built with `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build`, served from
`dist/` by a local static server that also answers the two endpoints
`src/main.tsx` awaits before `createRoot().render()`
(`/api/v1/runtime/config`, `/api/v1/auth/*`) and serves the precompressed
`.br`/`.gz` siblings the build emits. Driven by Playwright with the Chromium in
this environment, cache disabled, a fresh context per run.

**Two independent readings of the same window, deliberately:**

| | what it reads | what it cannot read |
|---|---|---|
| **A — compositor frames** | CDP `Page.startScreencast`, every swapped frame decoded and classified pixel-by-pixel (a frame is "white" when no channel falls below 242). "First non-white frame at T" is the card's claim taken literally. | Nothing between two captured frames. |
| **B — Paint Timing** | `first-contentful-paint`. Per spec it excludes a root background-colour paint, so it is an exact reading of "first *content*" and an upper bound on "first non-white pixel". | Anything painted that is not text/image/SVG/non-white-canvas. |

A and B agreed to within 2-7 ms on every run, which is the main reason to trust
either.

### Before → after

Three network profiles (CDP `Network.emulateNetworkConditions`). Both columns
are real production builds of the two trees, measured with the same instrument —
the "before" column was produced by checking `apps/console/index.html` back to
`f53a8d0ae`, rebuilding for real (mutation confirmed on disk *and* in
`dist/index.html`), then restoring and rebuilding (restore proven
byte-identical: `git hash-object` == `git rev-parse HEAD:apps/console/index.html`).

**Pure-white window, first non-white compositor frame, ms:**

| profile | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| localhost, no throttling | **1516 – 1655** | **194 – 230** |
| 20 Mbps / 80 ms RTT | **2307 – 2407** | **284 – 342** |
| Fast 4G (4 Mbps / 70 ms) | **5661 – 5716** | **570 – 588** |

3 runs each. The Fast-4G column is the card's reported 3-6 s band, so the
staging report reproduces. 2.21 MB across 64 requests were fetched before one
pixel of content appeared.

The screencast itself costs CPU (every frame is JPEG-encoded), and the fixed
build emits far more frames because the indicator animates — 361 vs 54 on Fast
4G. With the screencast off and only the performance API read, the after column
is **lower**: 120-144 ms on localhost, 548-556 ms on Fast 4G. The table above is
therefore conservative.

### The residual ~550 ms on Fast 4G is render-blocking CSS, not this fix

The built shell carries three `link rel="stylesheet"` tags in the document head (largest
362 KB raw / 47 KB gzipped). A pending render-blocking stylesheet blocks the
document's first paint no matter where the markup sits, so it floors what any
HTML-layer indicator can do. Filed as #6379 — making that non-blocking changes
FOUC semantics for the whole app and is not a tier-1 change.

## 2. Where the indicator ships, and the proof it can paint during the gap (T3)

The gap **is** the load of the JavaScript, so an indicator that travels inside
that JavaScript becomes visible exactly when it is no longer needed. All three
parts — markup, styles, script — are in `apps/console/index.html`.

Three separate proofs, in increasing strength:

1. **Grep on the built artifact.** `boot-splash` appears 17× in
   `apps/console/dist/index.html` and in **zero** files under `dist/assets/`
   (`grep -rl 'boot-splash' apps/console/dist/assets/` → empty).
2. **The served bytes.** `e2e/console-boot-indicator.spec.ts` fetches the
   document over HTTP and asserts the element, an inline `style` block carrying
   `#boot-splash`, and a **classic inline** `installBootSplash` script are all
   present, with the script ahead of the element it themes.
3. **Causal — the one that actually settles it.** With `page.route('**/*.js',
   abort)` no chunk ever arrives, and the indicator still renders: visible,
   `elementFromPoint` at the viewport centre is not `body`, computed background
   is neither transparent nor `rgb(255,255,255)`, and the mark has real
   geometry. A component test cannot tell "the skeleton exists" from "the
   skeleton can paint during the gap"; blocking the bundle can.

⚠️ One thing this PR **corrects** rather than asserts: I first wrote "the splash
precedes the application entry in document order". That is **false of the built
artifact** — Vite hoists the `script type="module"` entry tag into the document head, ahead
of the body element entirely (measured on `dist`: entry at offset 7925, element at 8626).
It is harmless, because a module script is *deferred* and cannot execute before
the parse finishes, but the assertion passed against the source while being
false of what ships. It is replaced by the ordering that survives the build (the
classic script precedes the element) plus a separate check that the entry stays
a module.

## 3. `LoadingScreen` is not doubled up and not delayed (T2)

The indicator is removed on React's **first commit** into `#root` — not on a
timer, which would either uncover the white page again or sit on top of a
rendered app. A `MutationObserver` callback is a microtask checkpoint on
React's commit task, so removal lands in the frame the app first paints.

- **Never two at once:** every measured run reports the indicator still mounted
  at the instant React commits (`splashUpAtMount=true`, 9/9), and
  `expect(page.locator('#boot-splash')).toHaveCount(0)` immediately after mount.
  So the window is covered end to end with no frame between the two.
- **Not delayed:** an A/B on the **identical artifact** — same bytes, the only
  difference being an injected `#boot-splash{display:none}` that suppresses the
  paint:

  | | first contentful paint | React's first commit |
  |---|---|---|
  | localhost, indicator painting | 120 – 144 ms | 1166 – 1363 ms |
  | localhost, indicator suppressed | 1172 – 1540 ms | 1149 – 1506 ms |
  | Fast 4G, indicator painting | 548 – 556 ms | 5577 – 5648 ms |
  | Fast 4G, indicator suppressed | 5632 – 5688 ms | 5606 – 5656 ms |

  Mount time is indistinguishable between the two; only first paint moves. This
  also happens to be the cleanest red/green available: one artifact, one
  variable.

`LoadingScreen` keeps ownership of the init screen and its ten-language copy.
The indicator ships **no text at all** — the i18n packs live in the bundle it is
waiting for, so a string here would be untranslatable English in a ten-language
product, and a product name would mean waiting for `GET /api/v1/runtime/config`.
It is `aria-hidden` for the same reason: it carries nothing a screen reader
could use, and the accessible copy arrives with `LoadingScreen` a moment later.

The colours are the app's own `--background` / `--primary` tokens from
`apps/console/src/index.css`, inlined because that stylesheet is in the bundle
too — which is what makes the window *non-white* rather than merely non-empty.
The boot canvas reads `ThemeProvider`'s own `vite-ui-theme` key (and
`prefers-color-scheme`) so a dark-theme user does not trade a white flash for a
light one; it writes `data-boot-theme` rather than the `light`/`dark` class the
provider owns, and removes the attribute with the splash.

## 4. What the committed tests can and cannot see (T1)

The claim is a **timing** property, and neither committed instrument reads
pixels. Stated plainly:

| instrument | sees | does not see |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/console/src/__tests__/bootSplash.test.ts` | the shipped document's structure; the script executed against a real DOM (theme resolution incl. storage-blocked, handoff on first commit, no removal while `#root` is empty) | any timing at all — no compositor, no meaningful clock |
| `e2e/console-boot-indicator.spec.ts` | order (`first-contentful-paint` vs React's first commit) and cause (indicator renders with every chunk blocked), against the production build | pixels; whether the frame was *literally* white |
| the screencast run in §1 | pixels, frame by frame | it is not in CI — it needs a throttled profile per run and is chromium-only |

**Red before, green after** — both committed files, run both ways:

- Cut the `div id="boot-splash"` element out of `apps/console/index.html`
  (609 bytes; mutation confirmed by sha256 before/after and by counting
  occurrences outside comments): `bootSplash.test.ts` → **2 failed, 13 passed**.
  Restored (`git checkout HEAD --`, blob hash back to
  `5fc051c127a9650224d45c0c758f4d8a8b5527d1`): **15 passed**.
- Cut the same element from the served `dist/index.html` and confirm the server
  returns 0 occurrences: all **3 e2e tests fail**, the timing one with
  `first-contentful-paint (1344ms) must precede React's first commit (1276ms)`.
  Restored (sha256 back to `821fe1c2…`): **3 passed**.

One test-authoring trap worth recording, because it had assertions passing for
the wrong reason: the prose in `index.html` **describes** this markup and
contains the tag-shaped literals for the splash element, the React root and the
body element itself, so every positional search found the comment first. Comments are now
stripped before any offset is taken — the same hazard
`insecure-origin-crypto.placement.test.ts` already records for script tags.

## 5. Gates — run at `57d3de441`, working tree clean

Gate set derived from the job step lists under `.github/workflows/` (`ci.yml`
type-check + test + e2e jobs, `lint.yml`, `control-bytes.yml`,
`changeset-presence.yml`, `changeset-guard.yml`, `vi-mock-specifiers.yml`,
`shell-escape-residue.yml`, `performance-budget.yml`) intersected with the paths
this PR touches. Exit codes captured before any pipe; the quoted text is each
gate's own verdict line.

| gate | exit | its own verdict line |
|---|---|---|
| `vitest apps/console/src/__tests__/{bootSplash,insecure-origin-crypto,insecure-origin-crypto.placement,runtimeConfigBootDedup,localizationBootDedup}` | 0 | `Test Files  5 passed (5)` / `Tests  48 passed (48)` |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console run lint` | 0 | (clean; eslint `--format json`: 2 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings) |
| `pnpm run lint:root` | 0 | (clean) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console run type-check` | 0 | (clean) |
| `pnpm run type-check:e2e` | 0 | (clean) |
| `pnpm run check:control-bytes` | 0 | `✅ check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 5249 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |
| `pnpm run check:vi-mock-specifiers` | 0 | `✅ check-vi-mock-specifiers: OK (3760 tracked source file(s), 2072 test-named; …)` |
| `pnpm run check:shell-escape-residue` | 0 | `✅ check-shell-escape-residue: OK (4/4 root(s) resolved …)` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 | `✅ 2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s): .changeset/console-boot-splash.md.` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-fixed.mjs` | 0 | `✅ All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group.` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | 0 | ✅ No changeset declares a "major" bump. |
| `node scripts/check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` | 0 | `✅ aggregate closure 3223.1 KB measured / 3266.6 KB ceiling (headroom 43.5 KB = 0.49x the 89.0 KB regression)` |
| `playwright test --project=chromium e2e/console-boot-indicator.spec.ts e2e/console-rendering.spec.ts` | 0 | `7 passed (8.9s)` |

`console-rendering.spec.ts` is in that list on purpose: it is the pre-existing
blank-page guard, and it still passes. Note the failure mode this change does
**not** alter — a bundle that never evaluates now shows a permanently pending
indicator instead of a permanently blank page, and that spec's `#root`-content
assertion still catches it either way.

Every `pnpm --filter` run above echoed its script name (`> @object-ui/console@17.6.0
lint …`), so none of them is the silent zero-match that exits 0 having run
nothing. `pnpm lint` repo-wide was not run locally — CI owns that run; the
narrowing here is complete for the changed paths rather than partial: `eslint.
config.js` configures no `project`/`projectService`, so type-aware linting is off
and this diff cannot change the verdict for any file it does not touch, and the
two owners of the changed paths (`apps/console`'s own `eslint .` and `lint:root`,
which covers `e2e/`) both ran green.

## Out of scope, filed separately

- **#6378** — a one-frame white flash **after** `LoadingScreen`'s first paint
  (40-230 ms), in 4 of 9 pre-fix and 3 of 9 post-fix full-boot runs. A different
  window from this card's; n=9 a side does not separate those two numbers, so
  read it as "roughly one boot in three, before and after".
- **#6379** — the render-blocking stylesheets in §1 that floor first paint at
  ~550 ms on Fast 4G. Every route out of it is structural (FOUC semantics for
  the whole app), which is why it is a card and not a rider here.

Neither is addressed here; both stay open.
